entities.summary: The Vienna Award was either of two arbitral decisions made by Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy awarding disputed territory to Hungary. Both decisions were made at the Belvedere Palace, in Vienna, just before and after the Second World War (1939–1945) started.First Vienna Award : Hungary received part of southern Czechoslovakia. This territorial change was declared null and void in the 1947 Treaty of Paris. Second Vienna Award : Hungary received Northern Transylvania from Romania. This was voided by the Allied Commission in the Armistice Agreement with Romania in 1944.
